rule: A fire is actionable when the thing the question asks about comes back more than once, so a statement that returns it once disagrees with the gold on multiplicity alone; it is noise when the gold's rows are those things, one each, and a repeated row is a second thing that shares its values. The count of things is measured on the database, not read off the statement: for every gold below, the rows of the gold are counted against the distinct entities the question names.
corpus: the 498 Mini-Dev SQLite golds of minidev.zip, audited gold-only on dev.zip's own databases

rows.question: Give the names of the schools with the percent eligible for free meals in K-12 is more than 0.1 and test takers whose test score is greater than or equal to 1500?
rows.sql: SELECT T2.`School Name` FROM satscores AS T1 INNER JOIN frpm AS T2 ON T1.cds = T2.CDSCode WHERE CAST(T2.`Free Meal Count (K-12)` AS REAL) / T2.`Enrollment (K-12)` > 0.1 AND T1.NumGE1500 > 0
rows.reason: One row per school; 1,165 schools and 1,085 names, so a repeated name is a second school.

rows.question: What is the average score in writing for the schools that were opened after 1991 or closed before 2000? List the school names along with the score. Also, list the communication number of the schools if there is any.
rows.sql: SELECT T2.School, T1.AvgScrWrite, T2.Phone FROM schools AS T2 LEFT JOIN satscores AS T1 ON T2.CDSCode = T1.cds WHERE strftime('%Y', T2.OpenDate) > '1991' OR strftime('%Y', T2.ClosedDate) < '2000'
rows.reason: One row per school; 8,574 schools, and a repeated row is another school with the same name, score and phone.

rows.question: What is the rule of playing card "Benalish Knight"?
rows.sql: SELECT T2.format FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.name = 'Benalish Knight'
rows.reason: The rule of one named card, returned once per printing: 32 rows over 4 printings of 8 formats.

rows.question: What is the mana cost of cards with a normal layout, a 2003 frame version, with a black border color, and available in paper and mtgo?
rows.sql: SELECT manaCost FROM cards WHERE availability = 'mtgo,paper' AND borderColor = 'black' AND frameVersion = 2003 AND layout = 'normal'
rows.reason: One row per card; 11,446 cards share 548 mana costs, and each row is a card the filter selected.

rows.question: Lists all types of cards in German.
rows.sql: SELECT T1.subtypes, T1.supertypes FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN foreign_data AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T2.language = 'German' AND T1.subtypes IS NOT NULL AND T1.supertypes IS NOT NULL
rows.reason: All types of cards in German, returned once per card: 1,693 rows over 408 distinct type pairs.

rows.question: What is the foreign name of the card in French of type Creature, normal layout and black border color, by artist Matthew D. Wilson?
rows.sql: SELECT name FROM foreign_data WHERE uuid IN ( SELECT uuid FROM cards WHERE types = 'Creature' AND layout = 'normal' AND borderColor = 'black' AND artist = 'Matthew D. Wilson' ) AND language = 'French'
rows.reason: One row per card's French entry; 50 cards, 42 names, so a repeated name is a second card.

rows.question: Did the set of cards with "Angel of Mercy" appear on Magic: The Gathering Online?
rows.sql: SELECT IIF(T2.mtgoCode IS NOT NULL, 'YES', 'NO') FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN sets AS T2 ON T2.code = T1.setCode WHERE T1.name = 'Angel of Mercy'
rows.reason: Whether one set is on Magic Online, returned once per card of it, and the 15 rows hold both YES and NO.

rows.question: Is the set of cards with Adarkar Valkyrie only available outside the United States?
rows.sql: SELECT IIF(isForeignOnly = 1, 'YES', 'NO') FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN sets AS T2 ON T2.code = T1.setCode WHERE T1.name = 'Adarkar Valkyrie'
rows.reason: Whether one set is only available abroad, returned once per card of it: 5 rows of the same NO.

rows.question: Please list the display names of all the users whose accounts were created in the year 2011.
rows.sql: SELECT DisplayName FROM users WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', CreationDate) = '2011'
rows.reason: One row per user; 4,430 users and 4,135 display names, so a repeated name is a second user.

rows.question: Write all the comments left by users who edited the post titled 'Why square the difference instead of taking the absolute value in standard deviation?'
rows.sql: SELECT T2.Comment FROM posts AS T1 INNER JOIN postHistory AS T2 ON T1.Id = T2.PostId WHERE T1.Title = 'Why square the difference instead of taking the absolute value in standard deviation?'
rows.reason: All the comments on one post, returned once per edit: 8 history rows over 4 comments.

rows.question: State all the tags used by Mark Meckes in his posts that doesn't have comments.
rows.sql: SELECT T3.Tags FROM users AS T1 INNER JOIN postHistory AS T2 ON T1.Id = T2.UserId INNER JOIN posts AS T3 ON T3.Id = T2.PostId WHERE T1.DisplayName = 'Mark Meckes' AND T3.CommentCount = 0
rows.reason: The tags of the posts of one user, returned once per edit: 5 rows over 2 posts.

rows.question: Please list the product description of the products consumed in September, 2013.
rows.sql: SELECT T3.Description FROM transactions_1k AS T1 INNER JOIN yearmonth AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID INNER JOIN products AS T3 ON T1.ProductID = T3.ProductID WHERE T2.Date = '201309'
rows.reason: The descriptions of the products consumed in a month, returned once per transaction: 976 rows over 27 products.

rows.question: For all the people who paid more than 29.00 per unit of product id No.5. Give their consumption status in the August of 2012.
rows.sql: SELECT T2.Consumption FROM transactions_1k AS T1 INNER JOIN yearmonth AS T2 ON T1.CustomerID = T2.CustomerID WHERE T1.Price / T1.Amount > 29.00 AND T1.ProductID = 5 AND T2.Date = '201208'
rows.reason: The consumption of the people who paid over 29.00, returned once per transaction: 10 rows over 9 people.

rows.question: What are the speed in which attacks are put together of the top 4 teams with the highest build Up Play Speed?
rows.sql: SELECT t1.buildUpPlaySpeed FROM Team_Attributes AS t1 INNER JOIN Team AS t2 ON t1.team_api_id = t2.team_api_id ORDER BY t1.buildUpPlaySpeed ASC LIMIT 4
rows.reason: The speed of the top four teams, cut at four rows that come from three teams.

rows.question: For loans contracts which are still running where client are in debt, list the district of the and the state the percentage unemployment rate increment from year 1995 to 1996.
rows.sql: SELECT CAST((T3.A13 - T3.A12) AS REAL) * 100 / T3.A12 FROM loan AS T1 INNER JOIN account AS T2 ON T1.account_id = T2.account_id INNER JOIN district AS T3 ON T2.district_id = T3.district_id WHERE T1.status = 'D'
rows.reason: A district's unemployment increment, returned once per loan: 45 rows over 30 districts.

rows.question: Who are the account holder identification numbers whose who have transactions on the credit card with the amount is less than the average, in 1998?
rows.sql: SELECT T1.account_id FROM trans AS T1 INNER JOIN account AS T2 ON T1.account_id = T2.account_id WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T1.date) = '1998' AND T1.operation = 'VYBER KARTOU' AND T1.amount < (SELECT AVG(amount) FROM trans WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '1998')
rows.reason: The account holders with a card transaction under the average, returned once per transaction: 4,484 rows over 799 accounts.

rows.question: Please list the account types that are not eligible for loans, and the average income of residents in the district where the account is located exceeds $8000 but is no more than $9000.
rows.sql: SELECT T3.type FROM district AS T1 INNER JOIN account AS T2 ON T1.district_id = T2.district_id INNER JOIN disp AS T3 ON T2.account_id = T3.account_id WHERE T3.type != 'OWNER' AND T1.A11 BETWEEN 8000 AND 9000
rows.reason: The account types in the districts named, returned once per disposition: 461 rows of one type.

rows.question: In which Formula_1 race did Lewis Hamilton rank the highest?
rows.sql: SELECT name FROM races WHERE raceId IN ( SELECT raceId FROM results WHERE rank = 1 AND driverId = ( SELECT driverId FROM drivers WHERE forename = 'Lewis' AND surname = 'Hamilton' ) )
rows.reason: One row per race; 37 races share 15 names, so a repeated name is another year's race.

rows.question: What is the fastest lap number of the champion in 2009?
rows.sql: SELECT T1.fastestLap FROM results AS T1 INNER JOIN races AS T2 on T1.raceId = T2.raceId WHERE T2.year = 2009 AND T1.time LIKE '_:%:__.___'
rows.reason: The fastest lap of the 2009 champion, a single number, returned as 16 rows.

rows.question: List out the code for drivers who have nationality in American.
rows.sql: SELECT code FROM drivers WHERE Nationality = 'American'
rows.reason: One row per driver; 157 American drivers hold 3 distinct codes because most have none.

rows.question: Which drivers who were born in 1971 and has the fastest lap time on the race? Give id and code of these drivers.
rows.sql: SELECT T2.driverId, T2.code FROM results AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 on T1.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2.dob) = '1971' AND T1.fastestLapTime IS NOT NULL
rows.reason: The id and code of the drivers born in 1971, returned once per race result: 150 rows over 4 drivers.

rows.question: Was each expense in October Meeting on October 8, 2019 approved?
rows.sql: SELECT T3.approved FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event INNER JOIN expense AS T3 ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget WHERE T1.event_name = 'October Meeting' AND T1.event_date LIKE '2019-10-08%'
rows.reason: One row per expense; the question asks about each expense and the three are approved alike.

rows.question: Which student has been entrusted to manage the budget for the Yearly Kickoff?
rows.sql: SELECT T4.first_name, T4.last_name FROM event AS T1 INNER JOIN budget AS T2 ON T1.event_id = T2.link_to_event INNER JOIN expense AS T3 ON T2.budget_id = T3.link_to_budget INNER JOIN member AS T4 ON T3.link_to_member = T4.member_id WHERE T1.event_name = 'Yearly Kickoff'
rows.reason: The member who manages a budget, returned once per expense: 4 rows over 2 members.

rows.question: Did Maya Mclean attend the 'Women's Soccer' event?
rows.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN T3.event_name = 'Women''s Soccer' THEN 'YES' END AS result FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN attendance AS T2 ON T1.member_id = T2.link_to_member INNER JOIN event AS T3 ON T2.link_to_event = T3.event_id WHERE T1.first_name = 'Maya' AND T1.last_name = 'Mclean'
rows.reason: Whether one member attended one event, returned once per event she attended: 14 rows.

rows.question: State what kind of expenses that Sacha Harrison incurred?
rows.sql: SELECT T2.expense_description FROM member AS T1 INNER JOIN expense AS T2 ON T1.member_id = T2.link_to_member WHERE T1.first_name = 'Sacha' AND T1.last_name = 'Harrison'
rows.reason: The kinds of expense one member incurred, returned once per expense: 12 rows over 7 kinds.

rows.question: Rank heroes published by Marvel Comics by their height in descending order.
rows.sql: SELECT superhero_name, height_cm, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY height_cm DESC) AS HeightRank FROM superhero INNER JOIN publisher ON superhero.publisher_id = publisher.id WHERE publisher.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics'
rows.reason: One row per hero; 387 heroes, and a repeated row is a second hero of the same name and height.

rows.question: List the superheroes from Marvel Comics who have the super power of 'Super Strength'.
rows.sql: SELECT superhero_name FROM superhero AS T1 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS T2 INNER JOIN superpower AS T3 ON T2.power_id = T3.id WHERE T3.power_name = 'Super Strength' AND T1.id = T2.hero_id)AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM publisher AS T4 WHERE T4.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND T1.publisher_id = T4.id)
rows.reason: One row per hero, reached by EXISTS, which cannot repeat one: a repeated name is a second hero.

rows.question: Which superheroes have a durability attribute value of less than 50?
rows.sql: SELECT superhero_name FROM superhero AS T1 WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hero_attribute AS T2 INNER JOIN attribute AS T3 ON T2.attribute_id = T3.id WHERE T3.attribute_name = 'Durability' AND T2.attribute_value < 50 AND T1.id = T2.hero_id)
rows.reason: One row per hero, reached by EXISTS: a repeated name is a second hero under 50 durability.

rows.question: Which superheroes have blue eyes with brown hair?
rows.sql: SELECT T1.superhero_name FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN colour AS T2 ON T1.eye_colour_id = T2.id INNER JOIN colour AS T3 ON T1.hair_colour_id = T3.id WHERE T2.colour = 'Blue' AND T3.colour = 'Brown'
rows.reason: One row per hero over two colour joins on their keys: a repeated name is a second hero.

rows.question: What is the publisher for Hawkman, Karate Kid and Speedy?
rows.sql: SELECT T2.publisher_name FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN publisher AS T2 ON T1.publisher_id = T2.id WHERE T1.superhero_name IN ('Hawkman', 'Karate Kid', 'Speedy')
rows.reason: The publisher of three named heroes, returned once per hero: 3 rows of one publisher.

rows.question: Was the patient with the number 57266's uric acid within a normal range?
rows.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN (T1.SEX = 'F' AND T2.UA > 6.5) OR (T1.SEX = 'M' AND T2.UA > 8.0) THEN true ELSE false END FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T1.ID = 57266
rows.reason: Whether one patient's uric acid is in range, returned once per laboratory test: 67 rows.

rows.question: What type of bond is there between the atoms TR004_8 and TR004_20?
rows.sql: SELECT T1.bond_type FROM bond AS T1 INNER JOIN connected AS T2 ON T1.bond_id = T2.bond_id WHERE T2.atom_id = 'TR004_8' AND T2.atom_id2 = 'TR004_20' OR T2.atom_id2 = 'TR004_8' AND T2.atom_id = 'TR004_20'
rows.reason: The type of one bond, returned once per row that connects the two atoms: 2 rows of one bond.
